verdicts.title: The #895 fix's new public field and new failure mode never reached the auditing reference
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified in the current tree. Code: packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/_coin_flip.py declares `dataset_size: int | None = None` as a public dataclass field (documented in the class docstring Attributes) and `def train_indices(self, dataset_size: int | None = None)` which falls back to the recorded size and raises ConfigurationError only when neither is available. packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/attacks/_helpers.py:_scoring_loader (lines ~150-175) raises ConfigurationError for (a) `len(dataset) != coin_flip.dataset_size` ('dataset length (N) does not match the dataset size (M) the CoinFlip was constructed from; scoring requires the full concatenated dataset, not a training subset or split') and (b) canary indices outside [0, len(dataset)). Docs: docs/reference/auditing.md CoinFlip attribute table (around :238-243) still lists exactly num_canaries / canary_indices / in_indices / out_indices with no dataset_size; :248 still shows `cf.train_indices(dataset_size) -> list[int]` with the argument presented as required and the body text 'All indices except held-out canaries' with no mention of the recorded default; the loss_scores Raises block (:92-94) and gradient_scores Raises block (:148-150) still enumerate only batch_argnums / batch_size / collate_fn (+ reference_scores InputTypeError) and neither mentions the dataset-size mismatch or the out-of-bounds error. grep over docs/reference/auditing.md and docs/user-guide/auditing.md finds no occurrence of 'dataset_size' or of the mismatch wording. `git show --stat e6e3d478` touches only two source files and three test files, no docs. The reference page is hand-written prose (not mkdocstrings-generated), so nothing regenerates it. Genuine but low-impact docs drift: the code fails loudly with a self-explanatory message, so the only cost is that the documented API surface is incomplete. Not a duplicate of a specific open issue; #775 ('Reconcile documentation and citations with post-remediation code') is the natural umbrella but its open child #845 is the citation sweep, and this fix landed 2026-09-03, after that scope.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user calls loss_scores/gradient_scores with a filtered or subset dataset and hits `ConfigurationError: dataset length (N) does not match the dataset size (M) the CoinFlip was constructed from ...` (or the canary-index out-of-bounds variant). The message itself is clear, but neither scorer's Raises block in docs/reference/auditing.md mentions this failure mode, the CoinFlip attribute table omits the public `dataset_size` field so there is no documented way to read back the recorded size, and `train_indices` is still documented as requiring an explicit dataset_size even though it now defaults to the recorded value. docs/user-guide/auditing.md mentions none of the three. Pure documentation incompleteness for a fix that landed 2026-09-03 with no docs change; no runtime or privacy impact.

verdicts.title: Dependency-confusion defensive registration on PyPI covers only 4 of the 10 published distribution names; the other 6 are free for anyone to claim
verdicts.reasoning: I re-queried PyPI for all 11 names myself. Defensive stubs exist for exactly four: opaque-accounting (999.9.9, opaque_accounting-999.9.9.tar.gz, uploaded 2026-08-12T15:05:40Z), opaque-auditing (15:05:27Z), opaque-optimizers (15:05:34Z), opaque-dpftrl (15:05:46Z) — all with the verbatim description 'This public copy of the package is a stub published on pypi.org designed to mitigate risks from Dependency Confusion...'. HTTP 404 for opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers and opaque-alignment, i.e. unregistered and claimable. pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json is an unrelated third-party project (1.0.0, 'python libopaque wrapper', Stefan Marsiske), so the umbrella name cannot be defensively held. All six unregistered names ARE really published: https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/<name>/ returns 200 for each, and ci.yml:241 / release.yml:132 publish every wheel to that index and never to PyPI. pyproject.toml workspace.members lists the ten package directories and README.md's package table publishes all the distribution names. Repo confirmed public (GitHub API: visibility public, private false). Severity lowered from high to medium: exploitation is not reachable from the primary documented install path, which uses `--index-url` (pip then never consults PyPI), and the JetBrains index is anonymously readable (verified) so users do not need `--extra-index-url`. The realistic vectors are narrower than claimed: bare per-package installs (`pip install opaque-engine`) appear only in AGENTS.md's installation matrix and not anywhere under docs/, plus any environment that adds PyPI as an extra index (pip merges candidates across indexes and prefers the highest version, so a 999.9.9-style release wins) or sets uv index-strategy to unsafe-best-match. So: a verified supply-chain registration gap with arbitrary-code-execution consequences, gated behind a user misconfiguration or a bare-name install, in a pre-1.0 research library.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers and opaque-alignment are all published on https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/ but return 404 on PyPI (verified today), while the team's own defensive 999.9.9 stubs cover only opaque-accounting, opaque-auditing, opaque-optimizers and opaque-dpftrl. Any third party can register the six missing names. Attacker code then runs when (a) someone installs a sub-package by bare name — the form AGENTS.md's installation matrix documents — or (b) an environment adds PyPI as an extra index alongside the JetBrains index (pip merges indexes and takes the highest version) or sets uv's index-strategy to unsafe-best-match. Because opaque-base and opaque-engine are transitive dependencies of every other wheel, one captured name reaches every Opaque install in such an environment. The documented `pip install opaque --index-url ...` path itself is not affected, since --index-url does not consult PyPI. Separately confirmed: the umbrella name `opaque` on PyPI is an unrelated project, so it can only be handled by documentation, not registration.

verdicts.title: Internal JetBrains infrastructure identifiers are committed in the public repository: an access-controlled TeamCity server hostname and an internal GCP Artifact Registry project
verdicts.reasoning: All factual links verified: .teamcity/pom.xml:18 is literally `<teamcity.server.url>https://jbr-fed.teamcity.com</teamcity.server.url>`; anonymous GET of that host returns 401; .teamcity/README.md describes the intended import ('Set `teamcity.server.url` in `pom.xml` ...', hosted agent pool `Linux-Large`) and settings.kts carries the pipeline id and `teamcity.agent.jbHosted` condition; .github/workflows/build-devcontainer.yaml:77 hardcodes `GAR_IMAGE: europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/gke-dev-dws-jbr/ml/opaque-devcontainer` (also used at :104/:120) right next to `vars.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` / `vars.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`; `git grep -i teamcity -- .github/` returns nothing, so the .teamcity tree is referenced by no active pipeline; the repository is public (GitHub API). The forward-reference point also holds: .teamcity/README.md states in the present tense that the pipeline 'replaces the GitHub Actions Linux amd64 test matrix', which has not happened, contrary to AGENTS.md's no-forward-references rule. Severity cut from high to low, however: neither identifier is a credential or grants any access. GCP project ids and Artifact Registry paths are routinely non-secret and are visible to anyone who can pull the image; the TeamCity host sits behind authentication and its name is trivially derivable from the org name, so the incremental reconnaissance value is negligible and there is no path from either string to compromise without an independent credential leak. What remains is real but is repository hygiene / release-readiness policy (completeness of the 'remove internal specifics' work, plus a dead prototype with a false forward reference), not an information-disclosure vulnerability.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Two internal infrastructure identifiers remain committed in the public repository after the 'remove JetBrains-internal specifics' work was closed: the literal access-controlled TeamCity server URL https://jbr-fed.teamcity.com in .teamcity/pom.xml:18 (host returns 401 anonymously) together with a 3-file unused Kotlin DSL prototype whose README forward-references a GitHub-Actions-to-TeamCity migration that has not happened, and the internal GCP Artifact Registry path europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/gke-dev-dws-jbr/ml/opaque-devcontainer hardcoded in .github/workflows/build-devcontainer.yaml:77. Neither is a credential and neither enables access on its own; the concrete consequence is that the internal-specifics cleanup is incomplete and a dead, misleading CI prototype ships to public readers. Both are configuration-hygiene fixes (move to a build property / repository variable, or delete the prototype), not a security incident.

verdicts.title: Public install documentation's "Extras" commands omit the registry index and resolve to an unrelated PyPI project named `opaque`
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Docs verified: README.md:67-72 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:19-27 teach `pip install opaque --index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` (and the uv `--index` form), and the Extras blocks immediately below (README.md:78-81, installation.md:33-36) show four bare commands with no index flag: `pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`. A grep for packages.jetbrains.team across README.md and docs/ returns only those four lines (README:68,72 and installation:20,27) — every other install instruction is bare, including docs/user-guide/index.md:9 ('Install with `pip install opaque` (plus `opaque[...]` extras)') and docs/alignment/trainers.md:319 (`pip install opaque[trl]`), which the finding did not list. PyPI `opaque` is confirmed to be version 1.0.0 'python libopaque wrapper' by Stefan Marsiske, while the real project is served only from the JetBrains index (verified: that simple index lists real opaque wheels anonymously). Actual reproduction in a clean venv: `pip install --dry-run "opaque[all]"` printed only `WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all'` and resolved to `Would install opaque-1.0.0 pysodium-0.7.18`, building the unrelated sdist's metadata in the process. I then installed a stand-in real `opaque` 0.15.0 (with auditing/all extras) into the same venv and re-ran: pip still reported `Would install opaque-1.0.0`, i.e. the extras command does replace an already-installed real Opaque, whereas the bare `pip install opaque` in the same state was a no-op ('Requirement already satisfied ... 0.15.0'). So the finding's 'overwrites the installed opaque distribution' claim is accurate specifically for the extras form. Severity kept at medium: the outcome is a broken/wrong environment with only a warning, it is fully user-visible on the next import, and no privacy guarantee is affected.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader following README.md or docs/getting-started/installation.md top to bottom installs the real Opaque from the JetBrains index, then copies the Extras line below it. Because `--index-url` does not persist across invocations, `pip install "opaque[all]"` resolves from PyPI, where `opaque` is an unrelated 'python libopaque wrapper' 1.0.0. Reproduced in a clean venv with pip 24.0: the command emits only `WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all'` and resolves to opaque-1.0.0 + pysodium-0.7.18; with a real `opaque` 0.15.0 already installed it still resolves to opaque-1.0.0, replacing it (the bare `pip install opaque` in the same state is a no-op instead). The user's `import opaque.dpsgd` then breaks, or a CI image built from these docs ends up with the wrong `opaque` distribution. Same hazard for `uv add`, and the same missing flag appears in docs/user-guide/index.md:9 and docs/alignment/trainers.md:319.
